newsitem.title: USA: Travelers/Aetna seen ready for deal sooner.
newsitem.headline: Travelers/Aetna seen ready for deal sooner.

text.p: Travelers/Aetna Property Casualty Corp has made such swift progress consolidating Aetna Inc's property-casualty business, it may be ready to make another big acquisition sooner than expected, analysts said.
Dean Witter analyst Michael Lewis said he expects Travelers/Aetna to make a big accretive property-casualty insurance acquisition in the next 12 months.
Lewis said he raised his price target on Travelers/Aetna to $45 from $37, on expectations of such an acquisition.
Lehman analyst Peter Wade said he believes a deal is likely at least within the next 18 months.
"My point is that the better they're able to assimilate the acquisition of Aetna, the faster they can move on to looking at other acquisitions," Wade said.
"I think the assimilation of Aetna is going faster than either they or investors could hope; consequently we should expect an acqusition sooner rather than later," he said.
Without issuing common equity, Wade said he believes Travelers/Aetna could spend about $1.5 billion on an acquisition, but noted that the company has few constraints on financing.
Potential targets would likely be predominantly commercial lines insurers, analysts said. But the size of a possible deal is not an issue for Travelers/Aetna.
"It's not a question of what they can do," Lewis said. "They can do sizable deals. It's a question of what becomes available and what they can acquire at a reasonable price," Lewis said.

Travelers Group Inc has an 82 percent stake in Travelers/Aetna. Travelers/Aetna was formed after Travelers acquired Aetna Inc's property-casualty business on April 2, 1996 and merged it with its own property-casualty operation.
Travelers earlier said it is ahead of its plan to achieve $300 million in annual cost savings at Travelers/Aetna by the end of 1997.
More than half of those targeted savings have been achieved after only nine months of operation, Travelers said.
